newsitem.title: USA: America West to start new booking program.
newsitem.headline: America West to start new booking program.

text.p: America West Airlines Inc said Thursday it had launched a new passenger booking program for travel agents that will help the carrier continue paying 10 percent commissions to agents while saving millions of dollars annually in computer reservations system (CRS) fees.
Travel agents will be asked to eliminate the use of "passive bookings" for which America West must pay various CRS fees, the airline said.
A passive booking is a duplicate or mirror booking of a passenger reservation, often created to generate itineraries or other support documents.
The airline said it will work with travel agents to show them alternative ways to use CRSs to accomplish the same work but avoid added fees.

"Our CRS fees have escalated 20 percent in the last two years," said Ron Cole, vice president-sales for America West. "If we're going to remain a low-fare, full-service airline and pay 10 percent commissions to the entire travel agency community, then we have to look to our travel agent partners for help in battling these costs."
America West continues to pay 10 percent commissions to travel agents despite a lower commission cap imposed by other carriers last year.
